name: Clifton Brown

summary.text: Clifton Brown is a carpenter running as an unaffiliated candidate for Colorado's 3rd Congressional District.
He earned a high school diploma from Cherry Creek High School in 1976.
His campaign platform centers on ending gerrymandering by eliminating congressional districts, campaign finance reform, and housing affordability.

positions.quote: Alaska contains one of the largest old growth forests on the planet and is now being threatened by the trump administration and dirty thieves that support him.
positions.note: Statement concerns protecting the Tongass-area old-growth forest from the current administration's development/logging policy rather than explicitly addressing sale or transfer of federal land; inferred opposition to land sales given his stated concern for protecting federal land from exploitation.

research_notes: Brown's Ballotpedia survey and campaign site (ruhero.com) describe a platform of ending gerrymandering by abolishing congressional districts entirely, banning PAC/corporate money and outside income for officeholders, capping interest rates at 12%, a 32-hour workweek, and cutting military spending/closing foreign bases. None of these map cleanly onto the 25 statements without stretching (his redistricting position is about eliminating districts outright, not about Colorado's independent commission versus mid-decade redraws, so it was not coded against the redistricting-commission statement). No position found on abortion, guns, immigration enforcement, taxes, or any Colorado ballot measure specifically.
